diction, multi-view stereo, and multi-view pose estimation

ness of Pow3R at exploiting all available information. The

1. Introduction
Building general models for 3D perception that can unify
different 3D vision tasks such as depth estimation, key-
point matching, dense reconstruction or camera pose pre-
diction, remains a complex and exciting open challenge.
Traditional Structure from Motion (SfM) approaches such
as COLMAP [82] do not apply pre-learned priors, so each
scene must be optimized independently. On the other hand,
most learning-based approaches focus on specific 3D vi-
sion tasks such as depth completion [40, 74], monocular and
stereo depth estimation [68], pose estimation [102, 125] or
novel view synthesis [41, 61]. While these dedicated ap-
proaches have been successful to some extent, this trend
contrasts with other domains such as natural language pro-
cessing where a single model like ChatGPT [65], trained
with a vast collection of data, solves a range of different
tasks without requiring re-training.
While some models
like CroCo-v2, DINOv2 or Stable Diffusion [23, 76, 108],
trained on large image datasets, have served as learned pri-
ors for other tasks, including 3D vision ones, they are still
far from multi-purpose foundation models like ChatGPT is
for NLP.

DUSt3R [105] marked a significant step forward in
regression-based 3D foundation models. DUSt3R performs
3D dense reconstruction from uncalibrated and unposed im-
ages, solving many downstream vision tasks at once with-
out the need for fine-tuning. Its success can be attributed to
two main factors: (i) its use of a pointmap representation,
which provides flexibility over its output space and enables
to regress camera parameters, poses and depth easily and
(ii) its use of a transformer architecture that exploits power-
ful pretraining combined with a vast amount of 3D training
data. Despite its huge success, DUSt3R [105] and its suc-
cessor MASt3R [46] are extremely limited in terms of their
input space, i.e. they only take RGB images. Yet, in prac-
tice, many real-world applications do provide extra modal-
ities such that calibrated camera intrinsics, sparse or dense
depth from RGB-D sensors or LIDAR, etc. This raises the
question of how best to exploit additional input modalities,
and whether this not just boosts performance but also en-
ables new capabilities, such as obtaining the full depth from
sparse point clouds of SfM or LiDAR.
In this paper, we introduce Pow3R, a new 3D feed-
forward model that empowers DUSt3R with any subset of
priors available at test time such as camera intrinsics, sparse
or dense depth, or relative camera poses. Each modality is
injected into the network in a lightweight fashion. To al-
low the model to operate under different conditions at test
time, random subsets of input modalities are fed at each
training iteration. As a result, we obtain a single model that
performs on par with DUSt3R when no prior information
is available but outperforms it when it exists. Our model
also gains new capabilities as a by-product: for instance,
the camera intrinsics input allow to process images whose
principal point is far from the center, thus allowing to per-
form extreme cropping, e.g. for performing sliding window
inference. As a side contribution, our model directly out-
puts the pointmaps of the second image in its coordinate
system, allowing faster relative pose estimation. To sum
up, our contributions are:
• Pow3R is a holistic 3D geometric vision model capable of
taking any subset (including none) of camera intrinsics,
pose and depthmaps with corresponding input images.
• Extensive experiments demonstrate an important boost in
performance over DUSt3R which cannot exploit priors,
yielding state-of-the-art results in three benchmarks.
• By predicting the same pointmaps in two different camera
coordinate systems, we can achieve more accurate rela-
tive pose, orders of magnitude faster.
2. Related work
Structure-from-Motion and MVS. SfM [20, 21, 33, 39,
82] builds 3D sparse maps by optimizing camera parame-
ters using only RGB images. Traditional approaches con-
sists of handcrafted pipelines to match keypoints [7, 9, 32,
55, 77], form pixel correspondences across multiple im-
ages, determine geometric relations, and perform bundle
adjustment to optimize camera locations. Recently, SfM
has incorporated learning-based approaches leveraging neu-
ral networks as components [5, 15, 53, 80, 89, 95, 104, 117],
but it remains brittle to outliers and challenging condi-
tions. Likewise, multi-view stereo (MVS) aims to recon-
struct dense 3D surface through handcrafted pipelines based
on triangulation from multiple viewpoints [27, 28, 83].
Learning-based approaches have also been incorporated for
MVS to reconstruct 3D from few images [36, 45, 64, 87,
109, 115], and more recently by adopting the RAFT archi-
tecture [59] or using generic Transformers [13]. In contrast,
the recent DUSt3R framework [46, 105], upon which we
build our approach, departs from these methods altogether
by defining a simple and unified neural framework to 3D
reconstruction based on the paradigm of pointmap regres-
sion. The idea is that, ideally, learning-based MVS should
be capable of reconstructing 3D from a few images without
strictly requiring the availability of camera parameters.

**Structured Highlights for the Research Paper:**

---

### **Core Innovation**
The research introduces **Pow3R**, a novel 3D vision regression model that seamlessly integrates diverse input modalities, such as camera intrinsics, depth maps, and relative poses, into a single network. Built upon the foundation of the **DUSt3R** framework, Pow3R employs a **transformer architecture** leveraging pre-trained weights to enhance performance. A key innovation is the ability to utilize any combination of input modalities at test time, enabling the model to handle scenarios like extreme cropping and faster relative pose estimation.

### **Technical Approach**
- **Transformer Architecture**: Utilizes a transformer-based architecture for efficient processing and leveraging powerful pre-training.
- **Modular Input Handling**: Injects various input modalities (e.g., RGB, depth, camera parameters) into the network in a lightweight manner.
- **Random Subset Training**: During training, random subsets of modalities are used, allowing the model to adapt to different conditions and leverage available priors effectively.
- **Pointmap Regression**: Predicts pointmaps in two camera coordinate systems, facilitating accurate relative pose estimation and enabling faster processing.

### **Quantitative Findings**
- **State-of-the-Art Performance**: Experiments demonstrate significant improvements in depth estimation, monocular and stereo depth prediction, and multi-view pose estimation tasks.
- **Metrics**: Results are measured using metrics like RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) for depth accuracy and F1 scores for pose estimation, showcasing Pow3R's superior performance when prior information is available.

### **Limitations & Assumptions**
- **Training Dependency**: Requires sufficient training data for each modality to ensure effective learning.
- **Computational Efficiency**: Processing multiple modalities may impact computational efficiency, though the model maintains high accuracy.
- **Prior Quality**: Performance benefits are contingent on the quality and availability of prior information.

### **Domain Impact**
- **Versatility**: Pow3R unifies various 3D vision tasks, offering a single model that can handle diverse inputs and scenarios.
- **New Capabilities**: Enables extreme cropping, faster relative pose estimation, and processing uncalibrated images, enhancing practical applications.
- **Theoretical & Practical Impact**: Theoretically, it bridges the gap between learning-based and optimization-based methods. Practically, it opens new possibilities for 3D reconstruction in applications requiring high-speed processing and versatile input handling.

---

This structured overview highlights Pow3R's core contributions, technical underpinnings, and practical implications across various domains.
